page: Microsoft Azure E16d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 614 GB of bundled local storage and runs under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks place the E16d_v5 in the average tier across multiple workloads. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1899.39 and a multi-core score of 15536.33, while the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores reached 1638.0 and 9964.0 respectively. Memory performance is highlighted by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 834.28 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 56.93 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrated a static web serving throughput of 21.56 GB/sec and processed 14.9 million Redis SET operations per second. Large-scale LLM inference is limited, with the 7B model achieving 11.63 tokens/sec for text generation, while the 70B model is unsupported.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E16d_v5 offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive applications that require local scratch space without the overhead of external storage. The inclusion of 614 GB of local storage alongside 128.0 GB of RAM makes it highly suitable for database operations, caching layers, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. It is well-suited for workloads such as relational databases, Redis deployments, software compilation, and medium-scale data processing tasks.
